notice: Illustrative example built from ATLAS research. Course names come from Minerva's catalog as found on 4 Nov 2026 and are not yet checked against the live catalog. Not admissions advice.

start.prompt: Which part of Minerva pulls you in?

options.label: Natural Sciences
options.whatYouDo: Study how the physical and living world works, from particles to planets.
facts: Physics lives here, as the Matter and Energy concentration. Minerva has no separate physics major.
options.keepsOpen: Calculus and other Computational Sciences courses come along for the physics track.

options.label: Computational Sciences
options.whatYouDo: Study computation, mathematics and data as tools for hard problems.
facts: Math lives here, as the Mathematics concentration. Minerva has no separate math major.
options.keepsOpen: Minors let you keep a science interest alongside.

y1-ns.note: Everyone takes these. No choice yet.

y1-cs.note: Everyone takes these. No choice yet.

y2-ns.prompt: Your core starts with one physics course. Which lean?

options.label: Physics of the Universe
options.whatYouDo: Physics at the scale of stars and galaxies.
facts: NS110U Physics of the Universe
Then the shared core: NS111 Implications of Earth's Cycles, NS112 Evolution Across Multiple Scales, NS113 Chemical Structure and Reactivity
options.keepsOpen: Either physics course counts toward the Matter and Energy prerequisites.

options.label: Physics of Life
facts: NS110L Physics of Life
Then the shared core: NS111 Implications of Earth's Cycles, NS112 Evolution Across Multiple Scales, NS113 Chemical Structure and Reactivity
options.keepsOpen: Either physics course counts toward the Matter and Energy prerequisites.

items: CS110 Problem Solving with Data Structures and Algorithms

y3-ns.prompt: Pick a concentration. Your capstone starts this year too.

options.label: Graduate study
options.whatYouDo: A master's or Ph.D., often in research.
facts: 43.5% of Natural Sciences graduates were in an advanced degree six months out (n = 46, classes of 2019 to 2025)
Example: a Natural Sciences and Computational Sciences graduate went on to a Ph.D. in Geochemistry at Caltech

options.label: Work
options.whatYouDo: Straight into a science or science-adjacent job.
facts: 41.3% were in full-time work six months out (n = 46)
Roles the majors page names: researcher, lab technician, science consultant, computational biologist, bioinformatician, environmental educator
options.keepsOpen: Graduate study later, with work experience behind you.
